comparisons.peer_summary: The year-on-year decrease in All Other operating loss was attributed to the absence of the $1.4 billion Arm acquisition termination cost incurred in fiscal year 2023, partially offset by an $839 million increase in stock-based compensation expense in fiscal year 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA disclose the financial performance of their 'All Other' segments, which consist of non-core or miscellaneous operations. Intel reports a total 'all other' cost of sales of $1.8 billion, noting a decrease from the prior year driven by lower revenue from specific businesses like Altera and Mobileye. NVIDIA reports an 'All Other' operating loss, explaining that the year-on-year improvement (decrease in loss) was primarily due to the absence of a $1.4 billion Arm acquisition termination cost incurred in 2023, partially offset by increased stock-based compensation. While Intel focuses on the revenue-driven cost decrease and NVIDIA highlights the one-time charge elimination, both disclosures address the drivers of financial results in their residual 'All Other' business units.

comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm discuss the drivers of 'cost of sales' in their segment results. Intel attributes a decrease in 'all other' cost of sales to lower 2024 revenue from Altera and Mobileye. Qualcomm discloses that its QTL EBT margin expansion was primarily due to lower cost of sales driven by a decrease in amortization expense related to acquired patents, alongside higher revenues. Both companies identify specific components (revenue volume for Intel, patent amortization for Qualcomm) impacting their respective cost of sales metrics.
